key: Hard is thy love to win: thou art a Steer to him who longs for steers: Be to one craving steeds a Steed.
s: Near the end of a long hymn to Indra, among songs likened to cows lowing for their calves, the singer turns to his friendship; Sāyaṇa, on 6.45.26, takes that friendship as one that cannot be destroyed, and the ‘Steer’ as the giver of cattle.

evidence.words: हे इन्द्र “तव त्वदीयं “सख्यं सखित्वं “दूणाशं दुर्णाशं नाशयितुमशक्यम् । अतिदृढमित्यर्थः । अतो हे वीर वीरयितरिन्द्र गव्यते गामात्मन इच्छते त्वं “गौरसि गवां प्रदाता भवसि
evidence.gloss: O Indra, thy friendship is dūṇāśa, hard to destroy, impossible to destroy: very firm, is the meaning. Therefore, hero, to one who wants cows for himself thou art a cow (gauḥ), the giver of cows.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 6.45.26, at [485,26]). Plain sense faithful: 6.45.25 and 6.45.28 liken the songs to mother cows calling to their calves, and 26 turns to Indra’s friendship (sakhyam, Griffith’s ‘love’). Sāyaṇa on 6.45.26 (rev 273533, 2020-09-17 per the API) glosses dūṇāśa as impossible to destroy, very firm, and gauḥ as gavāṃ pradātā, giver of cows, by figure of effect for cause; Griffith’s note 26 and Wilson both report the same. The sentence does not go beyond this. entry-check ok.
